candidate.title: ClickSeq
candidate.scope: The single ClickSeq RNA-to-cDNA library-preparation architecture in the assigned Illumina schematic, resolved with the original 2015 ClickSeq implementation. Four depicted transformations lead from RNA through azido-terminated ss cDNA and click-adaptor coupling to an amplified cDNA library. Parallel molecule examples belong to one route, not separately processed branches. The title and matching collection-page caption identify ClickSeq only; associated kit names and the CoVaMa background citation do not identify alternative target workflows. No unshown optimization, size-selection, sequencing or analysis operation is added.

features: Biological target and reverse-transcription template are RNA.
The drawing uses purple strands with left-hand 5′ labels. The primary implementation begins with unfragmented sample RNA; no fragmentation operation is depicted.

states.label: Semi-random primers and AzNTP/dNTP mixture
features: Semi-random primers contain six random nucleotides and a constant Illumina 3′-adaptor region, called P7 in the catalogue.

These are added synthesis substrates/primers; they are not another biological input or workflow branch.

states.label: RNA-containing synthesis material with 3′-azido-terminated cDNA fragments
features: RNA-derived cDNA intervals are created by random-position priming and stochastic termination, rather than cleavage of the original RNA.

The figure retains purple RNA templates alongside shorter light-blue cDNA segments, N3-marked ends and opposite green/magenta primer-associated segments. This records the reaction material without requiring a particular RNA–DNA hybrid state.
cDNA has a blocked 3′-azido end and retains its primer-derived adaptor sequence at the opposite end.

states.label: 5′-hexynyl-modified Illumina click adaptor
features: DNA oligonucleotide with a reactive 5′-hexynyl alkyne group; called the Illumina 5′ adaptor in the primary paper and P5 adaptor in the catalogue.
Orange short segments with terminal black multiple-bond symbols are drawn next to the N3-bearing cDNA ends in the click-ligation panel. These depict the complementary reaction partner.

evidence.rationale: P5 is catalogue nomenclature for the click-adaptor side; the primary paper independently identifies the reactive 5′-hexynyl end.

states.label: Click-ligated ss cDNA with two Illumina adaptor regions
features: Post-ligation boundary is resolved from primary full text: each represented ss cDNA has the primer-derived adaptor on one side and the covalently joined click adaptor on the other.
The former 3′-azido cDNA end and adaptor 5′-alkyne participate in cycloaddition, forming an unnatural triazole-linked backbone at the junction.

The diagram displays N3 and alkyne symbols as reaction partners at the click step; those symbols are not evidence that free reactive end groups remain at the completed junction. See correction_click_product.

evidence.locator: Click-ligate alkyne-modified adaptor: orange oligos with terminal black multiple-bond symbols lie beside the N3-marked ends of light-blue cDNA. The following arrow leads to continuous orange/blue/green/magenta molecules.

evidence.quote: Upon the addition of ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) and tris(benzyltriazolylmethyl)amine-conjugated copper(I) ions (Cu-TBTA) as catalysts, the 3’-azido-blocked cDNA fragments are ‘click-ligated’ to the 5’-hexynyl adaptor via copper(I)-catalysed azide-alkyne cycloaddition11 (Figure 1B).
This process generates random single-stranded cDNA fragments from the original RNA that are flanked by the 5’ and 3’ Illumina adaptors, but that contain an unnatural DNA backbone.
The bulky triazole linkage (Figure 1B) can be read through by common DNA polymerases such as OneTaq polymerase (NEB) and Klenow DNA polymerase, albeit inefficiently.

states.label: PCR-amplified Illumina-compatible cDNA library
features: The final diagram label is cDNA library, represented by continuous orange/blue/green/magenta lines.
The primary paper resolves the PCR product as double-stranded DNA generated from the click-ligated ss cDNA; the one-line glyphs do not specify final strandedness.

The sequenced carrier is amplified DNA containing sampled RNA-derived insert sequences flanked by Illumina adaptor regions. The endpoint supports a downstream sequencing interface; sequencing itself is not drawn.

Capture into the library is incomplete because click ligation and especially polymerase read-through of the triazole junction are inefficient in the tested implementation. The product is not a complete census of original RNA molecules.

evidence.locator: PCR amplify and following rightward arrow to cDNA library: continuous colored molecule glyphs retain orange segments at the left and green/magenta segments at the right; reactive end labels are absent.

evidence.quote: Consequently, the click-ligated cDNA can be used directly in a PCR reaction to generate a cDNA library using Primers #3 and #4 (Table S1).

While approximately 10 % of the 3’-azido-blocked cDNA fragments in Figure 2B could be ligated to an alkyne-modified oligo, the conversion of this triazole-linked ssDNA into a double stranded DNA via the read-through of the triazole-linkage seems to be far less efficient.
evidence.rationale: This is evidence for incomplete capture and inefficient conversion in the tested implementation, not a universal efficiency specification or an added recipe setting.

operations.label: Add semi-random primers and AzNTPs - dNTP mixture
operations.description: The added semi-random primers initiate reverse transcription at positions along unfragmented RNA. cDNA extension incorporates ordinary nucleotides until AzNTP incorporation terminates the chain, creating RNA-derived cDNA intervals with blocked 3′-azido ends and a primer-derived adaptor on the opposite side.
operations.mechanism: Randomly primed reverse transcription with stochastic incorporation of chain-terminating 3′-azido-2′,3′-dideoxynucleotides. The primary paper calls this synthesis stage RT-PCR; it is the RNA-to-cDNA transformation preceding the separately depicted final PCR.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is copied into cDNA inserts sampled between a priming position and a termination position. The source RNA and DNA library are different physical molecules; one insert need not span a full starting RNA. The primer introduces an Illumina adaptor interface.

operations.label: Purify single-stranded cDNA
operations.description: Recover the single-stranded azido-terminated cDNA from the synthesis material while retaining its blocked end and primer-associated adaptor. The drawing drops the RNA templates; the primary account specifies removal of unincorporated AzNTPs before click ligation. Internal cleanup steps are outside the depicted block.
operations.mechanism: Purification of cDNA before adaptor coupling; the chemistry of RNA removal is not specified by this schematic.
operations.information_effect: The RNA-derived sequence carrier remains ss cDNA. Purification prepares its reactive 3′ end for the next operation without introducing another sequence association.

operations.label: Click-ligate alkyne-modified adaptor
operations.description: React the purified 3′-azido cDNA fragments with the 5′-hexynyl-modified adaptor. The completed product is adaptor-flanked ss cDNA containing a triazole junction; this product identity is supplied by the paper because the reaction panel still draws the N3 and alkyne reactants separately.
operations.mechanism: Copper(I)-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition covalently joins the cDNA end to the adaptor. Copper catalyst and reducing reagent reported in the paper enable the coupling and are not biological substrates, separate workflow branches or new operations.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second Illumina adaptor interface to the RNA-derived insert without joining two biological inserts. The substrate-specific coupling helps suppress artifactual chimeras, but the paper reports nonzero residual artifacts.

operations.label: PCR amplify
operations.description: Use click-ligated ss cDNA as a PCR template to produce an amplified cDNA library. The primary paper explains that conversion to double-stranded DNA requires polymerase read-through of the unnatural triazole junction, resolving the interface between the click reaction and the continuous final product glyphs.
operations.mechanism: Adaptor-primed PCR using polymerase activity capable of copying the specific triazole-linked template. The demonstrated read-through is inefficient; this schematic does not establish compatibility of every polymerase or modified backbone.
operations.information_effect: Amplified DNA carries the sampled RNA sequences into the sequencing library. Downstream reads can support sequence coverage of viral RNA and mRNA and detection of junctions within captured inserts, as demonstrated by the primary paper. Inefficient capture and amplification mean that library copies are not a direct count of all original RNA molecules; apparent junctions still require interpretation in view of residual artifacts.

checks.rationale: Independent image and source review supports the complete candidate at its declared schematic/original-implementation scope. All four depicted transformations, seven material states, ten material routes, single target scope, two reference assessments and chemical interpretation have been checked individually below. RNA is the biological template, cDNA is the copied sequence carrier, and amplified DNA is the library. The two rows are molecule examples under one route, with no labeled independent fractions, compartments, split, pooling or alternative. Primer/nucleotide addition and adaptor coupling are genuine joint reactions, not compressed independent processing. The 3′-azido and 5′-alkyne reactants become a triazole-linked ssDNA template before PCR; this is consistent across the corrected state and both adjacent flows. Incomplete capture and residual artifacts remain qualified. No consequential unsupported claim or omitted diagram transformation remains.
